item.content:encoded:
Love it, but just one thing bugs me (well, other than the anachronistic cellphone thing) - was there not even a cursory attempt made to paint the cat face back onto the statue and see if that returned it to a more happy-go-lucky state? Or was it simply thought to be too much of a risk in case it was to be washed off once again, and containment was better served by having it angry but locked up rather than happy-but-potentially-angry and wandering around?

(Still, happy AND locked up would be the better combo… with containment procedures demanding that no water, or water based cleaning materials, be introduced to the cell, to minimise the chance of the cat face being washed off).

In any case, still now definitely headcanon that this is the true origin of 173.

I mean, I'd more likely expect them to have totally worked out the smartphone technology and got replicas up and running sometime in the late 80s at worst, but that one particular point throws doubt on it. Well, that and Clef using a PDA in the Researcher Wars…

But yeah, it did sort of stand out.

Of all the bits and bobs of this article that make fun of the whole lolfoundation aspect of series 1, one section in particular makes numerous references to tales/examples of the lolfoundation doing what it does best. Two of those references are to Clef-Kondraki and The SCP-050 Prank War. As such a simple edit would be to include the following in-line links to these documents:

Recommend editing the following:

Before this revision was ordered, the Site Director requested that Foundation Senior Staff decommission SCP-173-J due to its new properties, as the staffers are, to quote the Director’s requisition letter, “awesome and dreamy and wacky”. However, the request was denied; all Senior Staff were too busy chatting with, seducing, wielding, playing practical jokes with, or riding to victory various SCP objects. The Site Director identified this setback as “disastrous to the safety and integrity of the Foundation, but exactly as hilarious as they think it is”.
